note: CUET-fit judgements for NTA mode (data/nta_fit_scores.js). Written by scripts/nta-fit-merge.mjs from three independent judges per question under docs/brain/NTA-CUET-FIT-RUBRIC.md. Majority (2 of 3) type, unit and chapter override the engine's heuristic; NTA mode admits a question only when all three judged the current content, fewer than two raised a fit flag and the median fit score is at or above NTA_MIN_FIT_SCORE. A judge-dependent label, not evidence.
subject: general_test

judges.note: One-step ratio (120 / 40). Key correct. Odd 'seats per percentage point' framing; distractors 2, 0.3 and 4 are plausible slips.
One division (120/40) in a seats-per-point framing. Fair routine application; the framing is slightly unusual for CUET GAT.
One division (120/40) after a rate framing; 'seats per percentage point' wording is odd for CUET. Format 2 caps at 8.
Percentage points versus relative change, a key chapter idea. Key correct (1 pp; 1/6 = 16.7%). The 1% decrease distractor is a real trap. Newspaper framing is fair.
Percentage points versus relative change; options 1% and 1 pp are real misconceptions. Answer-pair options are wordier than typical CUET items.
Percentage points vs relative change (1 pp; 1/6 = 16.7%). Core percentage idea and a standard CBT trap; clean key-aspect test.

Same percentage-point versus relative-change idea as the unemployment item, with a 50 percent relative change. Clean; pair-style options cap format at 2.
Same percentage-point vs relative-change idea as the unemployment item. Option C is garbled, so discrimination is 2; no route.

Successive percentage change (compound, not additive): a standard CBT staple. The 30 percent additive trap is a real misconception.
Successive percentage change (1.10 x 1.20 - 1 = 32%). A recurring CBT staple; the additive 30% is a real trap.
Average speed over equal distances: 120 / 2.5 = 48. Key correct. The arithmetic-mean distractor 50 is a strong trap. Labelled easy but three steps.
Average speed over equal distances (harmonic mean, 48). The 50 option is the arithmetic-mean trap. Several steps to compute; fits 2 minutes.
Average speed over equal distances: a standard speed item in plain CUET style. 50 is the arithmetic-mean trap. No route claimed.
SI = 2000, CI = 2100, so CI is 100 more. Key A correct. D (200) is a plausible error. Type set to single_mcq; it is a comparison item in form.

Simple vs compound interest on Rs 10,000 (SI 2000, CI 2100). Two cases in the stem make it wordier than real items; format 2 caps at 8.
Total distance 120 over 3 h = 40; the columnist's 45 is wrong. Key B correct. The 'Case:' and 'columnist' framing is stylised, so format 2.
Average speed plus harmonic-mean naming plus a judgement of a columnist's claim. Top of the CBT range; naming the mean is peripheral for GAT. Key B is correct (40 km/h).
Average speed = 40 (harmonic). Naming the harmonic mean is beyond usual GAT wording and the 'Case:' framing is unusual; level 2 caps at 8.
Independence rule, both statements true; Reason explains Assertion, key A correct. Class XII probability sits near the edge of GAT scope; level and syllabus scored 2.
Independence product rule with its definition as Reason; both true and R explains A (key A correct). Probability sits at the edge of this chapter; AR format is rare in GAT.
Independence rule as assertion-reason. Probability is a Class XII idea, so level 2 caps at 8. Option B is a real trap.
Weighted-average turnout arithmetic under a news frame. Easy, two steps. Stem tests arithmetic, not current affairs, so chapter is Numerical Ability.
Weighted average of two turnout rates; 55 is the simple-average trap. Moved to Numerical Ability (pure percent maths). Contrived news framing, format 2.
Weighted average of three group inflation rates (answer 3.1%). Standard CUET-style weighted average. Easy. Option text repeats the key letter ("B About 3.1%").
Weighted average of three price changes; 3.5 is the simple-average trap. Moved to Numerical Ability. Economics-style basket wording, format 2.

Single-step percent increase (40 to 50 = 25%). Very easy for a 72 s slot. Stem tests arithmetic under a news frame.

CPI 100 to 104 gives 4%. Very easy, one subtraction and one percent. Option text repeats the key letter.
